note: Adapted from Snyder's (1959) original description of the new species (in English); only the (female) alate is described, the soldier not. The figures of the original measurement table are lost wholesale in the OCR, so the entry gives the morphological description only, without values, as stated here. The original gives no separate diagnosis for the species, only noting that it is larger than the other known Neotropical species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Female alate: head chestnut-brown and glossy, longer than wide, slightly concave at the cranial suture and sloping forwards, scattered with long hairs. Compound eyes black, large and not circular, their distance from the side of the head about equal to their diameter and their distance from the posterior margin about twice their diameter. Ocelli large and prominent, situated at one corner of the compound eye but close to it. Labrum pale chestnut-brown with short hairs. Antennae pale yellowish brown, 19-segmented, segments 3 and 4 short, ring-like and minutely hairy. Pronotum pale chestnut-brown, wider than the head and twice as wide as long, the anterior margin arcuately concave, the posterior margin very shallowly concave, the sides rounded, scattered with long and short hairs. Legs pale yellowish brown, tibiae yellowish brown, an arolium between the claws but not prominent. Wings pale yellow, the veins yellowish brown and minutely hairy; media close to the subcosta and reaching the tip of the wing; fore wing subcosta with 8 (mostly long) branches reaching the costal margin; cubitus nearer the subcosta than the lower margin of the wing, with 11 branches reaching the lower margin; wing scale 1.6 long. Abdominal tergites pale chestnut-brown, scattered with long and short hairs.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The figures of the original measurement table survive in the OCR only as row labels (total length of the alate with wings, total length without wings, head length to the tip of the labrum, greatest pronotum length, hind tibia length, fore wing length, compound eye long diameter, head width at the compound eyes, pronotum width, fore wing width), the value column being entirely lost, so no figures are recorded. The author notes that the species is larger than all 15 Neotermes species described from the Neotropical region. Type locality Rancho Grande, Aragua state, Venezuela, at 1100 m altitude, 25 April (month 4) 1955, F. Fernandez-Yépez and C. J. Rosales collecting a series of alates at the type locality; further specimens from km 25 on the Maracay—Choroni road (1500 m), El Pilar, Bolívar state (150 m), and Guayaraca, Auyantepui (1020 m). The holotype is a female alate, United States National Museum catalogue number 63257.
